A Program That's Redrawing the Geospatial Talent Map: HBCU Immersion in GEOIN

August 19, 2026 Abigail Hart, Geo Week News HBCU, geospatial intelligence, GEOIN, workforce development, GIS education, Harris-Stowe State University, GeoHornet Lab, diversity
Read the source article

Quick summary

A four-week summer immersion program brings students from Historically Black Universities and Colleges to St. Louis to develop geospatial intelligence skills, combining technical GIS training with community belonging to build the next generation of geospatial professionals.

Key takeaways

  • The HBCU Immersion in GEOIN (Geospatial Intelligence) program is a four-week summer initiative based at Harris-Stowe State University in St. Louis
  • Students work out of the university's GeoHornet Lab at T-REX, the city's downtown innovation hub
  • The program goes beyond teaching software — it develops people who will carry the geospatial industry forward
  • Former participants have pursued graduate GIS studies at Northwest Missouri State University
  • The program's philosophy is "people-first": starting with community, building real partnerships, and fostering belonging
